The permitted maximum daily flow limitation is equal to the design capacity of the wastewater treatment plant which is 0.3 MGD and is located in Section 25, T15S, R12E, SBB&M. The discharge consists of disinfected secondary treated sanitary wastewater. 2.A. Discharge of Wastewater Treatment and Controls The treatment system consists of an influent diversion box, three equalization tanks, an automatic bar screen, an oxidation ditch, and a secondary clarifier. Effluent is chlorinated using sodium hypochlorite solution and dechlorinated using a sodium bisulfite prior to discharge. chunks.text: The secondary clarifier is a 10-layer non-reactive system labelled from the bottom to the top. It has a total height of 4 m, and occupies a surface area of 1500 m 2 and a volume of 6000 m 3 . The tank is fed from the 6th, treated water is harvested from the 10th, and the settled sludge flows out from the first layer. A fraction of the sludge flows out of the system in the form of waste at a flow rate of 385 m 3 /d, corresponding to a biomass age of 9 days, while the other fraction is recycled externally to the first tank at a rate of 18,446 m 3 /d. The biological processes occurring in both biological reactors are simulated using the IWA Activated Sludge Model No. 1 (ASM1) proposed by [47] . This model uses thirteen state variables to track the fate of biodegradable, non-biodegradable, soluble, insoluble, nitrogen, and carbon materials. These state variables are linked to eight degradation bioprocesses occurring in biological reactors.

chunks.text: A pilot-scale system, consisting of a grit tank and microscreen for primary treatment followed by a SAF-MBR 2.0 for secondary treatment, was installed at the Codiga Resource Recovery Center (Stanford, CA), as illustrated in. The pilot-scale system treated municipal wastewater pumped from the Serra Street sewer on the Stanford campus for more than three years. Sewage was de-gritted in a grit tank then subject to primary treatment by screening through a 0.3 mm pore size microscreen (MS-28, Hydro International). The pilot-scale SAF-MBR 2.0 consisted of: (1) two AFBRs operated in parallel, hereafter referred to as AFBR 1 and AFBR 2, containing fluidized GAC biocarrier, and (2) a gas-sparged membrane tank equipped with ultrafiltration membranes. Recirculation of bulk fluid (twice the influent flow rate) between the three reactors enabled complete mixing and control of solids accumulation within the gas-sparged membrane tank.

chunks.text: A pilot-scale plexiglas Carrousel oxidation ditch was constructed, in which three semicircular channels were connected to four 1.15-m long straight channels. The ditch was 0.35-m wide and 0.5-m deep with a total working volume of 1.4 m 3 . Air was introduced from four 1-m long microporous aerator pipes located at the base of the second and third channels. The sketch of the reactor can be found in the supplementary information (SI). Experimental activated sludge was seeded from a steady-running SBR process in a municipal WWTP. The COD and NH 4 + -N concentration of synthetic wastewater were controlled at 250 mg L −1 and 50 mg L −1 , and pH was approximately 7.8 without adjustment. The liquor temperature was maintained at 22 ± 2 °C with a heating rod. Before getting into the inlet of the first channel, the influent and returned sludge were firstly pumped into a 50-L bioselector with continuous blending to avoid sludge bulking problem. The variations of HRT and SRT were achieved by altering the daily influent and sludge discharge rate.

Overall, stable TCE removal rates >90% were demonstrated by both R1 and R3 at all influent TCE concentrations, with effluent TCE concentrations frequently below the detectable limit (10 lg l À1 ; Table 1 ). These results are comparable with previous studies of the treatment of chlorinated alkenes, which reported efficient removal of tetrachloroethene (PCE) up to concentrations of 50 mg l À1 in an upflow anaerobic sludge bed bioreactor, operated at room temperature (Prakash and Gupta, 2000) , and 98% PCE removal using an anaerobic attached film expanded bed (AA-FEB) process operating at low temperature, but only up to a loading rate of 12 mg l À1 (Carter and Jewell, 2003) .

chunks.text: Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) represent a diverse array of water treatment technologies that have generated significant research attention and utilization in a range of water and wastewater treatment applications over the years [1] . Many of the potential and demonstrated applications of AOPs are related to the treatment of industrial wastewater effluents, including those generated from hospitals, slaughterhouses, distilleries, textile mills, and chemical processing plants [2] . Depending on the source, industrial effluents can contain a mixture of complex pollutants, including recalcitrant and toxic organic compounds such as aromatics, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, personal care products, and endocrine-disrupting chemicals. AOPs have been identified as an effective means to treat these complex effluents due to their ability to produce powerful oxidizing agents such as hydroxyl radicals ( • OH) insitu [3] . The strength and non-selectivity of • OH as an oxidizing agent enables the complete mineralization of a wide range of organic compounds at first order rates in the magnitude of 10 6 to 10 9 M − 1 s − 1 [4] .

chunks.text: The drying facility is located in a large Polish wastewater treatment plant and is composed of 4 lines. The scheme of one drying line is presented in Fig. 1 . Dewatered sludge is collected in a silo from where it is dosed to drum dryers. The temperature in the drum dryers is maintained at ca. 240-260 • C using hot oil. Sludge is uniformly distributed in the drum with paddles. The sludge retention time in the drier is 1-2 min, and the sludge layer in the drum is 1-2 cm thick. Water from the sludge is evaporated and flows as condensate with process air through a purification system composed of a Venturi orifice and two scrubbers, where it is then rinsed with the process water (secondary effluent from the wastewater treatment plant). chunks.text: Each anoxic reactor is followed by aerobic tanks approximately double in volume, with a combined aerobic volume of 12,900 m 3 . Treated wastewater from the aerobic reactors is recombined and distributed to the settling basins (nine rectangular, one circular), with a combined volume of 11,500 m 3 . The dissolved oxygen (DO) set point of the aerobic tanks is 2.4 mg/L, while the DO set point for the settling basins is 2.7 mg/L. Fig. 1 . A flow diagram of the secondary treatment reactors with our approximate sampling locations (circled X): A) anoxic reactors (denitrification), B) aerated reactors (nitrification and carbon oxidation), and C) secondary clarifiers (settling basins). The single circular settling basin is physically separated from the nine parallel rectangular ones, but receives the same flow and has the same retention time. Wastewater enters this section of the system from the primary clarifiers and flow equalization basins, and exits to the tertiary filters and disinfection contact basins. The dashed lines between the anoxic and aerated reactors are baffles, used to isolate the anoxic and aerobic reactors. Dotted lines represent internal circulation.

chunks.text: The secondary biological treatment consists of two carrousel-shaped biological reactors with suspended biomass, equipped with two horizontal aerators, which include nitrogen removal. Regarding the sludge line, a fraction of the solids settled in the secondary settler is purged to the sludge thickener. Previously to the band filter, the sludge passes through a homogenizer to be mixed with cationic polyelectrolyte and further dewatered in the band filter prior being stored in a silo. Calafell WWTP was built on 1994 to treat the wastewaters of the municipalities of Calafell and Bellveí and designed for 70,000 population equivalent with a maximum flow of 12,000 m 3 /day. After a primary treatment, wastewater is treated in two activated sludge reactors with extended aeration including nitrogen removal, followed by the secondary settler. From these units, the treated wastewater is directly discharged to the submarine sewage. Some differences are observed in the operation of the plant between winter and summer seasons due to fluctuations on the population and changes on the influent composition. A coagulation-flocculation treatment, only operated during summer, receives the wastewater after the screening step.

chunks.text: Based on a survey on pre-treatment measures for 17 full-scale AeMBRs, the following information deserves special attention (Itokawa et al., 2008) : 1) grit chamber, coarse and fine screenings are mostly essential for MBR operation to removal grits, large suspended particles and long fibers, with fine screening (3 mm for FS membrane and 0.5-1 mm for HF membrane) installed universally; and 2) using the "by pass sieving" method, which recycles part of the suspended sludge through a sieve, achieves the further removal of unfavorable substances accumulated in the bioreactor. These means can be extended to AnMBRs minimizing the presence of undesirable substances into the bioreactor while with adequate consideration of keeping strict anaerobic environment. A recent novel concept, referred to as wastewater pre-concentration (Ansari et al., 2016) , is still under investigation, but has shown great potential to enhance bioresource recovery and energy generation efficiency (Guven et al., 2019) , accompanied by a low volumetric flow rate and process footprint (Alvarado et al., 2020) .

chunks.text: An equalization tank was designed to maintain airflow and homogenize the incoming  wastewater, with a maximum volume of 30,000 m 3 and a depth of 4 m. In the biological step, the MBR bioreactor, as a prominent innovation in wastewater treatment, was designed with a total membrane surface area of 4200 m 2 and a porosity of cake layer equal to 0.15 m 2 . This design facilitates the degradation of both organic and inorganic substances, reduces sludge production, and produces high-quality effluent. Moreover, the tank volume was set at 9740 m 2 , and the backwash frequency and flow rate were assumed to be 30 s and 2000 m 3 /d, respectively. Then, the RO technology was implemented to enhance and complete the wastewater treatment process. The RO membranes, characterized by their small pore size, effectively reject molecules and ions, resulting in purified water. The RO system contained four vessels with a membrane area per element of 35 m 2 /element. The assumed recovery rate for the RO system was 60 %, meaning that 60 % of the feed water was treated and converted into purified water.
